modelspec.training.LearningRateSchedule.title: LearningRateSchedule
modelspec.training.LearningRateSchedule.description: How the learning rate varies over steps, settled by coordinator decision D50 of 2026-10-25 under the operator's grant of 2026-10-24, after Devlin et al. 2019. With t counting steps from 1 and steps the run's total, the rate is lr*t/warmup_steps for t <= warmup_steps and lr*(steps-t)/(steps-warmup_steps) after, lr being OptimizerConfig.learning_rate; it starts above zero, peaks at lr at step warmup_steps and reaches zero at the last step. warmup_steps = 0 means no warmup; warmup_steps >= steps is refused (E-TYPE-024, or a run error when --steps shortens the run). The host computes each step's rate in Binary64 and rounds it once to Binary32 (DESIGN.md § 2.1, § 6).

modelspec.training.OptimizerConfig.title: OptimizerConfig
modelspec.training.OptimizerConfig.description: Optimizer hyperparameters, recorded for reproducibility (DESIGN.md § 6.1). The AdamW fields are present exactly when kind is AdamW (Loshchilov and Hutter, decoupled weight decay); its first and second moments are a checkpoint's optimizer slots (DESIGN.md § 6.2).

learning_rate.description: The base learning rate; the peak rate when a schedule is present.

schedule.description: Present exactly when kind is AdamW, settled by coordinator decision D50 of 2026-10-25; SGD keeps its constant learning rate, as M0 has.

x-ess-invariants: ((kind == Sgd and not (defined(weight_decay)) and not (defined(beta1)) and not (defined(beta2)) and not (defined(epsilon)) and not (defined(schedule))) or (kind == AdamW and defined(weight_decay) and defined(beta1) and defined(beta2) and defined(epsilon) and defined(schedule)))

modelspec.training.OptimizerKind.title: OptimizerKind
modelspec.training.OptimizerKind.description: SGD from M0; AdamW with decoupled weight decay and a warmup schedule from M3, written `adamw(lr = F, weight_decay = F, beta1 = F, beta2 = F, eps = F, warmup_steps = N)` (DESIGN.md § 1, § 2.1, § 11 iteration 4; epic:bert-from-scratch).
